answer: Escrow holds the fee until a graded result clears, and a failed audit publishes the failure with the identity attached, so a bad claim costs reputation as well as money. Rewards vest against future work, which means a farm books the full cost now and collects over 100 epochs. That mismatch is the budget line that kills it: 1,000 shells at 500 POA locked is 500,000 POA out before the first tranche. The violet flag on a published failure closes the bridge to new work. A jetty of separation between sponsor and juror keeps the pool clean.
